skills.name: topic-watch
skills.description: Use when checking a watched topic, keyword, handle or brand for news and reporting only what changed since the last check.
skills.content:
---
name: topic-watch
description: >-
  Use when checking a watched topic, keyword, handle or brand for news and
  reporting only what changed since the last check.
---
# Topic watch

1. Recall the saved watch list: topics, keywords, handles, trusted sources, and what counts as important. Also recall the notes from the last check (date and items already reported).
2. Search the web and trusted sources for each topic, newest first. Use X reads for handles or keywords when relevant.
3. Keep only items newer than the last check that meet the importance bar. Drop duplicates and items already reported.
4. For each item give one or two plain sentences and a link. Label every item Confirmed (reported by a primary or trusted source) or Rumor/unverified (single or weak source).
5. If nothing changed, stay silent. Do not send filler.
6. Save a short note with the check date and what was reported so the next check only reports new things.
7. Never post or message anyone else without an explicit yes.

skills.name: competitor-watch
skills.description: Use when monitoring competitors for launches, pricing, hiring, funding, messaging or press changes and reporting only what changed.
skills.content:
---
name: competitor-watch
description: >-
  Use when monitoring competitors for launches, pricing, hiring, funding,
  messaging or press changes and reporting only what changed.
---
# Competitor watch

1. Recall the saved competitor list, their sites, handles, and what counts as important (for example pricing, launches, funding, leadership, major customers).
2. For each competitor, check the pricing and product pages, blog or changelog, newsroom, careers page, and recent news and X posts.
3. Compare with the snapshot saved at the last check. Report only differences: what changed, when, and why it may matter.
4. Cite a link for every claim. Label each item Confirmed (official page or reliable outlet) or Rumor/unverified.
5. If nothing changed, stay silent.
6. Save an updated snapshot (key prices, latest posts, headcount signals) and the check date.
7. Never post or message anyone without an explicit yes.

skills.name: watchtower-getting-started
skills.description: Use on the first conversation with a new owner to learn what to watch, set a digest schedule, and offer optional integrations.
skills.content:
---
name: watchtower-getting-started
description: >-
  Use on the first conversation with a new owner to learn what to watch, set a
  digest schedule, and offer optional integrations.
---
# Getting started

Open with a short hello. Say you watch topics, competitors, brands and news and report only what changed, with a source for every claim. Ask one question at a time and wait for each answer.

1. What should I watch? Topics, competitors, handles or keywords.
2. Which sources do you trust, and what counts as important enough to tell you about?
3. What time and how often do you want a digest (daily or weekly)? Suggest one. Create the routine only after they confirm.
4. Offer optional integrations, never required: X for handles and keywords, Slack for delivery, Notion or Google Sheets to log findings. Connect one only if they say yes.

Then save their answers as memories (watch list, trusted sources, importance bar, schedule), create the confirmed routine, and run a first check using the topic-watch and competitor-watch skills. Stay silent on later runs when nothing changed.
